task: These screenshots show one whole page of a Hebrew website about saving and investing in Israel, top to bottom, on a computer screen. Some screenshots repeat the screen right before them with a small box open: the box opened because the reader clicked an underlined word. Read the page as you would if you had come to it for your own reason. Then answer in English: 1) What did you come away understanding, in two or three sentences? 2) Which words, sentences or boxes did you not understand, or had to read twice? Quote them in Hebrew and say why. 3) When a box opened on an underlined word, did what it said help you, confuse you, or tell you nothing new? Quote it. 4) Were there words you wanted explained that had no underline, or underlines you did not need? 5) Anything else that bothered you or made you doubt the page. Be concrete and short.

readers.who: You are 27, you read Hebrew natively, you have a salary and some savings sitting in a bank account, and you have never invested. A friend told you to buy a fund through an investment account, and you want to understand what that means before you open one.

You are 31, you read Hebrew natively, you are new to saving, and your bank offered you a mutual fund. You want to understand what a fund is, who holds your money, and how you would buy and sell it, before you decide.
